detail: the authorization's signature recovers its payer, it pays the requirement the 402 published, the settle answer names it, and the chain at height moved exactly that transfer. three limits travel with every result of this format, whatever the verdict: see `coverage` for the reported_only rows resource_binding, facilitator_identity and rpc_trust, and the annotations limit_resource_binding, limit_facilitator_identity and limit_rpc_trust

resolved_key.origin: the authorization's from address; on an EVM chain the address is the identifier of the public key the signature recovers to

annotations.address_checksum_form: payTo is in EIP-55 checksum form; authorization.from is; this is a spelling and never a verdict
annotations.authorization_window_against_capture: not computed — this envelope supplies no `captured_at`, and the 402 object carries no instant of its own
annotations.settle_response_signed: no — the published SettleResponse has no signature member, so this object is the facilitator's unsigned word
annotations.chain_transfer_matches_authorization: from, to and value all equal the signed authorization
annotations.authorization_used_matches: authorizer and nonce both equal the signed authorization
annotations.block_at_height: the block at 51004854 has the receipt's blockHash 0xa4fa5d4f072b8abbcfe1a87cedabf5ece8d5073da67fdab8c56f3a0d2cae9956
annotations.settlement_instant: 1788799055 (2026-09-07T16:37:35.000Z), the timestamp of the block the receipt is in
